diagnosis: [REHEARSAL, not a real Claude answer] The health check's add-to-cart and checkout calls are failing with temporary errors from the hosting vendor (rate limiting / unavailable / gateway timeout). Real customers are reporting the same failures from their browsers.
root_cause: The shop's cart client gives up on the first error. It never retries the temporary errors the vendor documents, and it sends no Idempotency-Key, so a retried timeout could add a pizza twice.
fix_summary: Retry 429/502/503/504 and network errors up to 4 times with short backoff (honouring Retry-After), and send one Idempotency-Key per click, reused across retries, so each Add registers exactly once.
commit_message:
Retry temporary vendor errors with an idempotency key

The ordering API sheds load with 429/503/504. The cart client failed on the
first error, so customers' Add clicks were lost. Retry with backoff, honour
Retry-After, and reuse one Idempotency-Key per action so retries never
double-add.
risk: During a long outage customers wait a few seconds longer before seeing an error. Retries add some load on the vendor.

digest.headline: Your online ordering hiccupped, and it's fixed
digest.what_happened: Your website's ordering system was temporarily overloaded and rejected some requests.
digest.customer_impact: Some customers clicked 'Add' and nothing was added to their basket, so a few orders may have been lost during the problem.
digest.what_we_changed: The website now quietly tries again when the ordering system is briefly busy, and makes sure a pizza is never added twice.
digest.status: Fixed and tested. The automated test customer can order again.
